text:
anya: Quick heads-up — after the RBAC change this morning I'm seeing intermittent apac->eu TLS handshakes fail for svc-ingress. Errors look like "certificate verify failed" and a bunch of KMS unwrap denies. Anyone else?

mike: yep, spike around 08:12 UTC. stack shows: 
svc-ingress[handshake]: alert: peer cert CN mismatch
keystore: KMS UnwrapKey RPC failed: AccessDenied

raj: pasted the most common log lines we saw: 
[08:12:03] ingress=svc-ingress id=abc123 peer=svc-eu cert_status=verify_failed reason=chain_validation
[08:12:03] keystore request_id=keq-789 KMS=decrypt err=AccessDenied principal=rol-keystore-apac

audit-bot: Audit events for keystore unwraps between 08:00-09:00 UTC: event_ids=[evt-1122, evt-1123, evt-1124]. principals: rol-keystore-apac, rotator-service-account.

anya: I ran a quick openssl probe against the upstream LB to see the cert chain:
```
openssl s_client -connect svc-eu-internal:443 -servername svc.example.internal -showcerts
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=svc-eu-v2.example.internal
 1 s:/CN=intermediate-rotator
---
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
```
Chain looks incomplete / intermediate mismatch.

leo: Rotator ran in apac ~07:58 and pushed alias `svc-eu` -> `svc-eu-v2`. If ingress still requests `svc-eu` alias but KMS policy only permits `svc-eu-v2` unwrap that will fail. Could be a timing/alias-sync issue across regions.

mike: confirmed rotator logs show a small window where alias_table update (dynamo) was partial in apac.

raj: Can we get the KMS policy + rotator IAM quick diff? Suspect we tightened key usage to only allow rotator-service-account and rol-keystore-eu but not rol-keystore-apac after the RBAC change. Example policy lines:
```json
"Principal": { "AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::111:role/rol-keystore-eu"] },
"Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"]
```

anya: That matches what I skimmed. We removed rol-keystore-apac earlier today. If ingress in apac still tries to unwrap using that role (or a cross-role assume) it will get AccessDenied.

sre-oncall: Temporary mitigation options:
- quick rollback of RBAC removal for the specific rol-keystore-apac principal (fastest)
- add a route fallback to send apac traffic to eu-canary which still has old keystore mapping
- force rotator to re-sync alias table across regions (safe but slower)
Which do you want?

leo: I'd prefer re-sync first (less blast radius). If re-sync can't be completed in 15m, rollback the RBAC change for that role.

mike: I'll try re-sync now and run a simulated unwrap test.

mike: test results:
- before re-sync: aws:kms Decrypt -> AccessDenied for arn:aws:iam::111:role/rol-keystore-apac
- after manual re-sync of alias table: Decrypt succeeded, TLS handshakes started recovering (drop from 120/min -> 3/min).

anya: nice. Can someone open a follow-up to: 
1) audit all KMS key policies and cross-region principals (owner: sec)
2) add a rotator post-check that verifies alias table consistency across regions before cutover (owner: leo)
3) add a short-lived canary rollback plan into RBAC changes (owner: mike)
4) surface the specific audit events to SRE dashboard (owner: raj)

sec-bot: Created tracking issue: https://issues.example/RED-4928 (title: "keystore alias drift after RBAC change -> rotator sync check") assigned to [sec, leo, mike, raj].

anya: Also let's tighten TLS config in ingress: explicitly reject incomplete chains at edge, log cert fingerprint + alias on handshake failures so triage is faster. Add TLS1.3-only checkbox for internal service-to-service where feasible.

leo: will file infra PR for handshake logging + rotator pre-check.

mike: I'll draft a short postmortem blurb for the change rollback and update the RBAC runbook with a canary/observability checklist.

sre-oncall: Good remediation. We'll keep monitoring for 2h. If we see >5% handshake errors in that window re-open incident.

anya: Thanks team. Closing thread unless someone has new findings.

sec-bot: auto-note: remediation completed at 09:10 UTC, closed short-lived incident.
